title: Member with rigid end offsets (finite joint size): stiffness coefficients

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. The source gives the transformation of the stiffness of a plane member whose ends i, j are joined to the nodes 1, 2 by rigid links: F12 = T Gamma^T k' Gamma T^T Delta12, with offsets e_i = vector from node 1 to end i and e_j = vector from end j to node 2. Numeric instance chosen here: nodes 1 (0, 0) and 2 (5, 3) m; e_i = (400, 250) mm, e_j = (300, 350) mm, i.e. member offsets (400, 250, 0) at end i and (-300, -350, 0) at end j in the engine's convention (vector from the node to the flexible end); A = 6e3 mm^2, I = 200e6 mm^4, E = 200 kN/mm^2. Both nodes fully held; combinations U, V, R impose u2 = 1 mm, v2 = 1 mm, theta2 = 0.001 rad; the reactions at both nodes are columns 4, 5, 6 of the 6 x 6 matrix of Eq. 13.40 times the imposed displacement. First order, no shear deformation. Section properties the source does not give because they do not enter its plane model (Iy, J; A where stated) are placeholders that do not influence the targets.
